acceptance_boundary: Computational engineering study. No orbital prototype has been built, no vacuum thermal test has passed, no independent environmental advantage has been established. Every result is labeled: measured fact / literature parameter / assumed engineering input / simulation prediction.

c6_adversarial_corner_sweep.not_a_probability: All equally enumerated sensitivity corners, NOT an estimated probability distribution

claim_dispositions.C6_light_bus_11_93_kg_kW_screen_claim: REJECT (reopened and repaired): the 11.93 kg/kW screen claim rises to 19.44 kg/kW after four repaired omissions (+62.95% hidden mass), and to 20.66 kg/kW as full-system Arm G with end-of-life degradation.
claim_dispositions.pure_C3_general_purpose_orbital_parity: HOLD (terrestrial Arm A adopted for pure C3): at $500/kg launch the strongest orbital invention, Arm O, costs $272.65M/MW ($14960.66/kW-yr, 1.239x terrestrial Arm A at $220.0M/MW). Even at $0/kg launch Arm O is $257.28M/MW (1.169x all-in; 1.931x on non-silicon infrastructure). Parity needs launch <= $200/kg AND >=45% space-hardware/insurance reduction, or launch <= $65/kg AND 70% reduction.
claim_dispositions.round1_arm_N_direct_800V_HVDC_backside_O: LIMITED GO (component and architecture baseline): 14.58 kg/kW all-in, 58.34 t and 406.3 m3 per 4 MW in a single Starship launch; conversion loss 6.5% to 3.2%, die-to-radiator drop 11.5 K (T_rad 86.5 C at T_j 98 C).
claim_dispositions.round2_arm_O_20yr_reusable_spine_hotswap: LIMITED GO (strongest orbital architecture): 20-yr TCO $272.65M/MW vs $430.88M/MW for conventional Arm D (-36.7%) and $409.36M/MW for Arm B (-33.4%); re-entry Al2O3 -94.7% vs Arm D. Contingent on the untested dry-clamp TVAC coupon gates.
claim_dispositions.round3_arm_P_dual_use_C1_C2: LIMITED GO (orbit-advantaged dual-use workloads only; NOT pure C3 parity): gross $273.44M/MW, net $176.44M/MW ($11807.05/kW-yr) after an ASSUMED $4,850/kW-yr co-tenancy credit for 18% EO/SAR/sovereign relay duty. The credit is a hardcoded assumed input, not a market price.
claim_dispositions.spacex_starmind_ai1_75_kW_per_ton: HOLD FOR DENOMINATOR VERIFICATION: 75 kW/ton (13.33 kg/kW) matches 250 kW peak power on a ~3.33 t dry satellite; normalized to 175 kW continuous average it is 19.05 kg/kW. The public envelope itself is unstable across hosts (see PAPER.md Section 3.6).
claim_dispositions.stage0_non_energized_dry_clamp_TVAC_coup: BUILDABLE NON-ENERGIZED COUPON / HOLD FOR ENERGIZED TESTING: 12-shell AP214 MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP STEP model, Euler V-E+F=2 on all shells, 160.0 x 120.0 x 8.8 mm. Energized testing on hold pending external PE/EHS signoff.

evaluator_custody: Evaluation was performed by an internally separated harness (INTERNAL_SEPARATED_HARNESS); it has not been externally independently accepted. Internal test passage does not constitute external physical or third-party acceptance.

spacex_starmind_ai1_boundary_audit.boundary_verdict: SpaceX's 75 kW/ton (13.33 kg/kW) corresponds to 250 kW peak payload power on a ~3.33 t dry satellite. Normalized to 175 kW continuous average compute power on the same 3.33 t vehicle, specific mass is 19.05 kg/kW before wet propellant and replacement spares. The all-in continuous range is stated as assigned, 19.05-24.80 kg/kW; no code computes a point value inside that range.
